standard_prerequisites.name: The plane-curve setup
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the closed subscheme Z of the projective plane with principal ideal generated by the homogeneous form F.

standard_prerequisites.name: Codimension-one divisors on the plane
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the decomposition Z = sum a_i D_i into irreducible components with multiplicities, each D_i cut out by a homogeneous F_i.

core_obligations: Reducible F (proof lines 1886-1893): F = F' F'' gives a proper closed subscheme Z' of the same dimension inside Z, so Z is either non-reduced or reducible.

Irreducible F (proof lines 1894-1902): writing Z = sum a_i D_i, the products F and prod F_i^{a_i} cut out the same subscheme, hence differ by a scalar as generators of the principal ideal; F irreducible forces a single factor, so Z is a prime divisor, i.e. a curve.
proof_roadmap: Exhibit a proper sub-curve when F factors.
Decompose Z into weighted irreducible components with their equations.
Compare the principal generators up to scalars.
Conclude the prime-divisor property in the irreducible case.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes plane curves among principal subschemes of the plane by irreducibility of the defining form (statement lines 1879-1884). The proof (lines 1886-1902) is complete: the reducible construction, the weighted component decomposition, the scalar identification of generators, and the prime-divisor conclusion. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: a short two-direction argument with standard divisor inputs.
